data.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: vertical 2:3 Pinterest-native editorial image, alternate base photograph for a later restrained magazine headline
Primary request: Treat the exact loose tabletop sound button from Image 1 as a small postmodern office object discovered in an austere design archive. The image should feel like a witty interiors-magazine page about corporate honesty, not a catalog hero shot or advertisement.
Input images: Image 1 is the sole product-truth reference. Use only the loose product shown on the right, excluding the yellow package and pressing finger. Preserve one ordinary five-inch-wide device with one glossy red hemispherical dome, the existing white uppercase product word BULLSHIT centered on the dome, one low circular gray molded-plastic base, and small black speaker vents. The word is real product labeling.
Scene/backdrop: restrained institutional design archive with a long pale-gray powder-coated metal cabinet, a small piece of textured off-white paper underneath the loose button, one blurred chrome task lamp and one archival box in the distance with no writing.
Subject: the exact button sits naturally and loose on the cabinet at believable five-inch scale, not on a sales pedestal and not under a glass display dome.
Style/medium: highly realistic European design-magazine photography, tactile, dry, understated, subtle film grain.
Composition/framing: vertical 2:3, button low and slightly off-center, generous warm-gray wall above for later typography, quiet asymmetry, enough scale context to read as a small desk object.
Lighting/mood: cool north-window light with one warm reflection on the red dome, serious and quietly absurd.
Text: retain only the real product label BULLSHIT on the button exactly once. No other text, captions, headlines, labels, logos, badges, watermarks, or pseudo-writing.
Constraints: exactly one loose button; exact product silhouette, colors, label, and five-inch scale; physically grounded; no hand or retail package; no CTA, price, frame, collage, product-card layout, alarm mounting, detector implication, or conventional ad staging.
Avoid: centered showroom packshot, luxury pedestal, glass display case, giant button, emergency switch, wall mounting, duplicated product, pseudo-text, glossy commercial campaign styling, generic AI perfection.
data.changesFromParent: A deliberately different archive-object execution rather than a contextual presentation-room scene.
notes: Generated separately from the exact source reference and inspected at full useful resolution.
Rejected because the centered object display is less product-derived and more template-like than the meeting execution.
